common_name: Ardernei Variegated Lily of the Nile

planting.note: Divide and replant clumps in spring once frost danger has passed so roots can establish before summer bloom.

directions: One of the oldest named variegated Agapanthus selections, 'Ardernei' bears strap-shaped evergreen leaves broadly edged in cream-white above clean, pale blue trumpet flowers held in rounded summer umbels. The variegation is most pronounced in brighter light but can scorch in intense afternoon sun, so light shade in hot climates helps keep the leaf pattern crisp. Grow in well-drained, fertile soil and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain strong variegation and flowering.

common_name: Buckingham Palace Lily of the Nile

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in full sun; established clumps need little attention beyond annual feeding.

directions: Raised by UK breeder Dick Fulcher of Pine Cottage Plants, 'Buckingham Palace' produces exceptionally large, dense globes of deep violet-blue trumpet flowers on tall, sturdy stems well above the strap-shaped deciduous foliage. It is one of the larger-flowered hardy hybrids and has held an RHS Award of Garden Merit for its vigor and reliable late-summer display. Give it full sun and reasonably fertile, well-drained soil, and mulch over winter in colder zones since the foliage dies back.

common_name: Taw Valley Lily of the Nile

planting.note: Set out divisions in spring; this compact deciduous type suits smaller borders and containers.

directions: Named for the River Taw in Devon, England, where breeder Dick Fulcher developed it, 'Taw Valley' is a compact deciduous Agapanthus with rounded heads of clear mid-blue trumpet flowers held just above neat, narrow foliage. Its smaller stature makes it well suited to mixed borders and large containers where taller Agapanthus would overwhelm the scene. It is deciduous and reliably hardy where winters are not severe, dying back to a dormant rootstock each autumn.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in well-drained soil; this campanulatus selection tolerates colder winters than tender praecox types.

directions: A long-grown Dutch selection of the notably cold-hardy bell Agapanthus, 'Dokter Brouwer' bears nodding, deep violet-blue bell-shaped flowers in loose summer umbels above narrow, deciduous grey-green foliage. Because it derives from Agapanthus campanulatus, it tolerates considerably colder winters than praecox-type hybrids and dies back completely to a dormant crown in autumn. Grow in full sun with good drainage; it is a dependable, long-lived border perennial once established.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions in spring in part shade; this cultivar spreads readily once established.

directions: This variegated sport of the species parrot lily combines narrow leaves broadly edged in cream-white with the same curious dark maroon-and-green, parrot-beak-shaped nodding flowers streaked with blackish markings. The pale foliage brightens shaded woodland-edge plantings even before the late-spring flowers appear and holds its color best out of harsh midday sun. Like the plain species it spreads by creeping rhizomes and can be divided readily to increase stock or control its range.
